edits.before: - The slot is the trigger ref `merge:<owner>/<name>:<branch>` (for example `merge:tdoljyj/cross-memory-system:main`), and each such ref is a first-in, first-out merge queue. Join it only for the final round, once the pull request is ready and its merge approved where approval is needed: bring the default branch in and push first, then renew its claim with `trigger_refs` set to its current refs plus that ref (a renewal replaces the list). A merge ref never conflicts: the renewal succeeds, and the claim's `merge_queue` shows your `state` (`head`, `waiting`, `lapsed`, `out`), `position`, the `head` and who is `ahead`. Only the head holds the slot (`merge_slot_until`). Changing or adding a merge ref (other than its letter case) joins every queue of the claim again at the back. Where the resident CI runs, it may also put the claim into the default branch's queue itself (`merge:<owner>/<name>:main`, at the back) once it has admitted the current head of the pull request the claim is bound to, and extend the claim's lease while its CI runs, never past the hard deadline. The CI joins only a head that the resident's stage 8 has evaluated again and that passed the Owner review where one is required. Joining is not merging: merging still needs the required checks, and those require the Owner Grant where one is needed. Neither changes your `fence`, `lease_version`, `progress_ref` or renewal count, so your renewals stay valid. While the merge ref the CI added is on the claim, a renewal whose `trigger_refs` leave it out keeps it and your place; if your list then already holds the 50 refs a claim may hold, the renewal is refused with `work_claim_trigger_refs_invalid`. Once that ref has left the claim (a merge, a close or a CI failure gives the slot back), it is no longer the CI's: a ref you add yourself leaves with a renewal without it, as any of your refs, and stays yours when the CI rejoins it after a lapse. A renewal never shortens a longer lease the CI gave: it sets the later of the current expiry and 2 hours from now, within the hard deadline. When a CI extension has already brought the lease to the hard deadline, a renewal is still accepted: it records your progress, refs and write set, and the expiry stays at the deadline.
edits.after: - The slot is the trigger ref `merge:<owner>/<name>:<branch>` (for example `merge:tdoljyj/cross-memory-system:main`), and each such ref is a first-in, first-out merge queue. Join it only for the final round, once the pull request is ready and its merge approved where approval is needed: bring the default branch in and push first, then renew its claim with `trigger_refs` set to its current refs plus that ref (a renewal replaces the list). A merge ref never conflicts: the renewal succeeds, and the claim's `merge_queue` shows your `state` (`head`, `waiting`, `lapsed`, `out`), `position`, the `head` and who is `ahead`. The CI joins only a head that the resident's stage 8 has evaluated again, that passed the Owner review where one is required, and whose latest required checks have no confirmed terminal failure. The resident checks the exact head and required App pins before joining or extending; unreadable check inventories permit neither. A confirmed required-check failure returns an already queued PR's slot without releasing the work claim. Joining is not merging: merging still needs the required checks, and those require the Owner Grant where one is needed. Neither changes your `fence`, `lease_version`, `progress_ref` or renewal count, so your renewals stay valid. An explicit `trigger_refs` list replaces the whole list, including any merge ref the CI added: leaving that ref out leaves the queue while keeping the work claim active. Omitting `trigger_refs` preserves the current refs and queue place. Keeping a merge ref preserves its place under the normal renewal and lapse rules. A renewal never shortens a longer lease the CI gave: it sets the later of the current expiry and 2 hours from now, within the hard deadline. When a CI extension has already brought the lease to the hard deadline, a renewal is still accepted: it records your progress, refs and write set, and the expiry stays at the deadline.

edits.before: - While you wait, do nothing for the merge: do not bring the default branch in again or push for it, and do not tell the Owner. Renew about once an hour to keep your lease (2 hours) without spending the claim's 12 renewals, each with a new `progress_ref` such as `merge-queue:<UTC time>`, and read `merge_queue`; a renewal keeps your place. When you become head, bring the default branch in and push if it moved, wait for CI and merge, or enable auto-merge once the Owner has turned on "Allow auto-merge". Where the clued-admission App may write, the `clued-merge-executor` workflow brings the default branch into an admitted, non-`protected` head that fell behind, and merges an opted-in head once its CI workflows passed, their gated jobs run. Non-`protected` PRs also opt in when claim renewal `progress_ref` equals the full current head SHA (case-insensitive); `protected` PRs still need the body line `Clued-Auto-Merge: <head sha>`. After admission it reruns a successful gate-only run once, within the title's rerun limit. Opt in when you join, after merge approval; another head needs new opt-in unless only merging the default branch into the body-approved head. Keep the claim live until the merge, and record it in BeamingFace. Turn auto-merge off as soon as a CI required check fails or the merge is refused, and leave the queue then or when you stop: renew without the ref or release the claim (while a merge ref the CI added is on the claim, renewals keep it, so leave that queue by releasing the claim). Never stay in it while you wait on anything else.
